54	## Corrections to the 2026-11-14 reading (old to new)
55	
56	1. **Design language is not a blocker.** The previous table marked `i_design_language`
57	   as needed now ("the sample request cannot be written honestly without this"). The
58	   runtime does not gate a sample on a proposed choice, and the skill's own rule is that
59	   a scoped expert proposal can support an authorized sample while the final choice stays
60	   open. Side view is already confirmed (`i_view`), so the reference pose cannot be
61	   reproduced literally in any case; the proposal only names which reference properties
62	   the side-view figure carries. New reading: not blocking; the sample is the trial of this
63	   proposal; the owner can override it, and an early answer changes the readability
64	   landmarks (see 4). Status stays **proposed**.
65	2. **A hidden contract prerequisite was missing.** `C` requires `li`. Added `i_lighting`
66	   (observed) so the contract can be written as soon as the two owner answers arrive.
67	3. **The runtime gate is narrower than the earlier note implied.** Only choices linked
68	   through the sample output's contract (`C.ch`) gate `t_sample`, and for a sample phase
69	   `observed`/`proposed` values are acceptable; only `unresolved`/`conflict` block.
70	   Confirmation is required for `t_scout`/`t_medic`/`t_family` (production/delivery),
71	   which also need an evidence-backed decision record `D`. The earlier note did not
72	   distinguish these, and so overstated what the owner must confirm before a sample.
73	4. **Two saved criteria presume answers that are still open.** These are plan defects to
74	   fix in the same commit that saves the contract, not now, because their correct text
75	   depends on the path the owner chooses:
76	   - `q_canvas`, `q_palette`, `q_outline` are worded against the **confirmed** canvas,
77	     palette and outline treatment. On the owner-confirms path that is right. On a
78	     delegated-trial path nothing is confirmed, so these three would be unsatisfiable for
79	     the sample; sample-specific copies worded against "the sample contract" (e.g.
80	     `q_sample_canvas`, `q_sample_palette`, `q_sample_outline`) must replace them in
81	     `f_sample.rq` before any candidate is evaluated. Production outputs keep the
82	     confirmed wording.
83	   - `q_readability` requires "separable head, torso and limb landmarks". The references
84	     have no head/torso split and no limbs (a single body block with two stalks, two eyes
85	     and, in reference.png, shoulder and base bars). The silhouette-readability method
86	     (`s_methods`) asks for *named identity landmarks*; the head/torso/limb list is the
87	     predecessor's assumption of a limbed figure, which is exactly what
88	     `i_design_language` leaves proposed. Proposed replacement text once the sample
89	     contract exists: "At native scale and at the target integer zoom, on light, dark and
90	     busy test backgrounds, the figure reads as a side-view character with an
91	     unambiguous facing direction, and the identity landmarks named in the sample
92	     contract remain separable." The landmark list is then written into the contract's
93	     own record (`C.nm` or the handoff) from the adopted construction.
94	5. **Palette confirmation is coupled to role differentiation.** `q_palette` is exclusive
95	   ("no colours outside it"). If the owner confirms the palette as exactly the reference
96	   colours and the role device later turns out to need an accent hue, the palette must be
97	   reopened. Recommendation: confirm the palette only together with the role device, or
98	   confirm it explicitly as the base palette with one reserved accent slot.

100	## Decision table
101	
102	Authority: who decides, and the saved status. "Needed now" means the next local
103	operation (saving the sample contract) cannot proceed without it. An answer adopts only
104	the choices it explicitly supplies; unasked rows keep their status.

106	| Choice (record) | Authority / saved status | Needed now? | Effect of the answer |
107	|---|---|---|---|
108	| Outline treatment (`i_outline`) | Owner; **conflict** between the two references (owner stated the disagreement) | **Yes** | See question 1. Decides whether `#25354A` is in the palette and what `q_outline` tests. The references contain two treatments; the owner has required neither. |
109	| Canvas size (`i_canvas`) | Owner; **unresolved**, explicitly deferred by the owner | **Yes** | See question 2. The references are 32 x 32 (observation, not a requirement). Lets `C.px` be written. |
110	| Game backgrounds (`i_backgrounds`) | Owner; **unresolved** | Helpful, not blocking | Turns the outline choice into an informed one (sheet: outline helps on busy mid-value fields, hurts on dark ones) and makes the readability review backgrounds representative instead of the agent's light/dark/busy test set. |
111	| Design language (`i_design_language`) | Owner; **proposed** by the predecessor (style swatch, not the body design) | No (corrected) | The sample trials this proposal. If the owner says the side-view figure must keep the reference's stalk-and-block body, the readability landmarks are the stalks, notch, eyes and bars; if a different construction is wanted, name it and the landmarks follow. |
112	| Lighting (`i_lighting`, new) | Owner; **observed** flat | No; supplies `C.li` | Observed from the references; the sample uses it as-is. Confirming it is only needed before production. |

The sample is the scout; an early answer lets the sample carry the device and lets the palette be confirmed once. |
116	| Palette (`i_palette`) | Owner; **observed** (3 reference colours) | Follows the outline answer | Confirming also adopts the exclusive rule in `q_palette`, which is a derived rule, not a brief statement. Confirm together with the role device. |

122	## Questions for the owner (necessary: 1 and 2)
123	
124	**1. Outline treatment for the sample and the family.** Which do you want?
125	
126	- (a) **Outlined**, as `reference.png`: flat 2 px `#25354A` contour that also carries the
127	  shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks. Unlocks: `i_outline` confirmed with your
128	  answer as source; palette can be confirmed as the three reference colours (plus any
129	  role accent); `q_outline` tests the contour and those interior landmarks.
130	- (b) **No outline**, as `reference-b.png`: flat teal silhouette with cream eyes. Unlocks
131	  the same, with the palette as two colours, but the shoulder, base and stalk landmarks
132	  that the navy carried must be re-authored (a second teal value or a cream accent) or
133	  dropped deliberately; say which, or let PIXL propose it for the sample.
134	- (c) **Delegate for the sample only**: PIXL picks one treatment as a recorded proposal,
135	  you decide after seeing the sample. Unlocks the sample contract now with `i_outline`
136	  moved to proposed; production still waits for your confirmation.
137	
138	If your levels are predominantly dark, the sheet favours (b); if they are busy or
139	mid-value, it favours (a); on light fields either works. Telling us the typical level
140	backgrounds answers `i_backgrounds` and informs this choice.
141	
142	**2. Canvas for the sample.** Which do you want?
143	
144	- (a) **32 x 32**, the references' canvas, carrying a figure about 18 x 25. Unlocks
145	  `i_canvas` confirmed and `C.px = [32, 32]`.
146	- (b) **Another size** you name. Note from the study: with a 2 px outline, a materially
147	  smaller canvas leaves little interior for the scout and medic to differ in; a materially
148	  larger one makes the 2 px contour read thinner than the references' weight.
149	- (c) **Delegate for the sample only**: PIXL trials 32 x 32 as a recorded proposal and the
150	  final canvas stays open, as your brief says. Unlocks the sample contract now with
151	  `i_canvas` moved to proposed; production still waits for your confirmation.
152	
153	**Optional, answer now if easy (not blocking):** is the side-view character meant to keep
154	the references' stalk-and-block body, or are the references a style swatch for a figure
155	you will let PIXL construct (`i_design_language`)? And how should the scout and medic be
156	told apart: accent colour, silhouette attachment, or both (`i_role_diff`)?
157	
158	## Specialist proposal for the trial sample (a proposal, not an owner requirement)
159	
160	If both answers are "delegate": outlined, 32 x 32, binary alpha, nearest sampling, flat
161	lighting, three-colour palette, one idle pose facing right (facing direction is a scoped
162	specialist choice for the sample; the engine can mirror it), body carrying the two-stalk
163	silhouette and eye placement of the references adapted to profile, with the shoulder
164	and base bars as the side-view torso landmarks. Rationale: it is the reversible option,
165	keeps every reference landmark available for role differentiation, and is the treatment
166	the sheet favours on busy and light fields. This proposal would not confirm any choice.
167	
168	## Exact next local operation and its prerequisites
169	
170	Once questions 1 and 2 are answered (or delegated), all of the following is executable
171	with the local runtime alone (Python 3.11+, Pillow, jsonschema are present; verified by
172	`readiness`):
173	
174	1. Save the owner's answer verbatim as a new project source file (e.g.
175	   `sources/owner-answers-<date>.md`) and add an `S` record for it.
176	2. Update intake: `i_outline` and `i_canvas` to confirmed (owner answer as source) or to
177	   proposed (delegated path, alternatives preserved in `wy`); `i_palette` to the
178	   resulting colour list (confirm only with the role device, or as base + reserved
179	   accent); `i_backgrounds` if supplied. Do not touch unasked rows.
180	3. Add `C` `c_sample` with `nm`, `px` (= `i_canvas.vl`), `pl` (= `i_palette.vl`),
181	   `vw = side`, `sa = nearest`, `al = binary`, `li` (= `i_lighting.vl`) and
182	   `ch = [i_canvas, i_palette, i_view, i_sampling, i_alpha, i_lighting, i_outline,
183	   i_design_language]`; set `f_sample.ct = c_sample`. The runtime requires each linked
184	   choice whose key names a contract field to equal that field's value.
185	4. On the delegated path, add the sample-specific `q_sample_*` criteria and the corrected
186	   readability text (correction 4), and swap them into `f_sample.rq`. On the confirmed
187	   path, apply only the readability correction. Either way this plan change must be
188	   committed before any candidate is evaluated.
189	5. Bump to revision 8, `validate --root <consumer root>`, then `commit` against the hash
190	   published by revision 7. `ready` should then list `t_sample`.
191	
192	Beyond that, the following are **not** available to the local runtime and were not
193	attempted here:
194

1	# Method research for the two open decisions
2	
3	Retrieved 2026-09-14 from the bundled PIXL knowledge library via `pixl_knowledge`.
4	These are the library's own words and source locators, recorded so the reasoning behind
5	this project's criteria is traceable. **A bundled method and its bundled proof-of-concept
6	receipt are context for this project, not proof about this project's assets.**
7	
8	## silhouette-readability
9	
10	Title: "Evaluate identity using silhouette and target backgrounds".
11	Applies to: characters, inventory icons, interactive props.
12	Sources: `training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md` lines 857-867 and 1563-1573;
13	`training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-ASSETS.md` lines 11-15.
14	
15	Requires: "Intended viewing scale, representative backgrounds and identity landmarks".
16	Checks: "Named identity landmarks remain visible at the target size."
17	Pitfalls the library states explicitly: "Silhouette alone cannot validate faces,
18	materials or fine symbols." and "No contrast ratio or component count proves aesthetic
19	quality."
20	
21	**Applicability here.** This is why the project's readability and role criteria are
22	declared with domain `visual` and mode `visual`, and why the scout/medic distinction is
23	stated as an observable landmark condition at native scale rather than as a pixel count.
24	It also means the outline question cannot be settled by measuring the references: the
25	library explicitly denies that component counts or contrast decide aesthetics.
26	
27	## edge-rhythm
28	
29	Title: "Audit stair-step runs without imposing one contour style".
30	Sources: `training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md` lines 1402-1431 and 857-867.
31	
32	Pitfalls the library states explicitly: "Not every uneven run is a jaggy; shape can
33	require an abrupt change." and "Mechanical contour smoothing can erase style and
34	identity."
35	
36	**Applicability here.** This is the direct reason the outline disagreement is retained
37	as a conflict for the user rather than resolved by the agent. The library's position is
38	that contour style is authored intent, so picking one reference over the other is a
39	style decision belonging to the project owner, not a cleanup the agent should perform.
40	
41	## integer-presentation
42	
43	Title: "Render at a declared logical grid and inspect device pixels".
44	Sources: `training/original-docs/PIXEL-ART-DEEP-RESEARCH.md` lines 907-919, 1293-1315,
45	1636-1638.
46	
47	Requires: "Logical resolution, camera convention and target viewport dimensions".
48	Pitfalls: "Nearest filtering alone does not constrain lighting resolution." and
49	"Noninteger scaling, arbitrary rotation and browser zoom can change displayed pixel
50	widths."
51	
52	**Applicability here.** The method requires a target viewport/display scale as an input.
53	This project has neither a canvas size nor a display scale, which is why the canvas
54	choice is recorded as unresolved together with a separate unresolved display-scale
55	choice, and why the engine criterion is declared but cannot be exercised.
56	
57	## Consequence for this session
58	
59	None of these methods supplies a value for the two open decisions. They establish that
60	the decisions are the owner's to make and that they are coupled, which is recorded in
61	`reference-observations.md`. No method was adopted into a design decision (`D`) this
62	session, and no proof was executed for one, because production has not been authorized
63	to start.
64

1	# Measured observations of the supplied references
2	
3	Measured 2026-09-14 with the bundled asset check and direct pixel reads, then inspected
4	visually at native scale and at 12x nearest-neighbour enlargement
5	(`work/reference-views/`). Measurements are mechanical; the style judgements below are
6	labelled where they are inference rather than measurement.
7	
8	## Identity
9	
10	| | reference.png | reference-b.png |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| sha256 | d997cade…70aa7 | e76b40ce…14a12a |
13	| canvas | 32 x 32 | 32 x 32 |
14	| visible pixels | 390 | 390 |
15	| visible bbox | x 7..24, y 3..27 (18 x 25) | identical |
16	| visible colours | 3 | 2 |
17	| fractional-alpha pixels | 0 | 0 |
18	| opaque components (4-connectivity) | 1 | 1 |
19	
20	## Shared, measured
21	
22	- Identical alpha mask. Every visible pixel in one is visible in the other.
23	- Binary alpha in both files: zero fractional-alpha pixels.
24	- Body colour `#56B5BC` (teal) and detail colour `#F4DDA2` (cream) in both.
25	- Two cream clusters, each exactly 3 wide x 4 tall: x 11..13 and x 18..20, both y 14..17.
26	  They read as eyes and are mirror-symmetric about the figure's vertical axis.
27	- The figure is bilaterally symmetric and front-facing, with two vertical stalks at the
28	  top separated by a notch.
29	- No anti-aliasing and no dithering in either file.
30	
31	## The outline disagreement, measured
32	
33	The two files differ in exactly 180 pixels, and every one of those differences is the
34	same substitution: `#25354A` (dark navy) in reference.png becomes `#56B5BC` (teal) in
35	reference-b.png. There is no other difference.
36	
37	- **reference.png**: a flat 2-logical-pixel navy outline fully enclosing the teal body.
38	  The two top stalks are 4 px wide and therefore rendered entirely in outline colour,
39	  with no teal interior. Two full-width navy bars at y 9..10 and y 26..27 read as a
40	  shoulder line and a base line. Outline is a single flat colour with no ramp.
41	- **reference-b.png**: no outline. Flat teal silhouette, cream eyes only. The shoulder
42	  and base bars and the stalk interiors disappear entirely, because they were drawn in
43	  the outline colour rather than as separate shapes.
44	
45	**Inference, not measurement:** the outline in reference.png is not decorative trim. It
46	carries interior structure (the shoulder bar, the base bar, and the solidity of the
47	stalks). Dropping it, as reference-b.png does, removes readable landmarks, not just the
48	contour. A decision for the unoutlined treatment therefore has to re-author that
49	interior structure in some other way — a second teal value, or a cream accent — rather
50	than simply deleting the outline colour.
51	
52	## Coupling between outline and canvas size, inference
53	
54	A 2 px outline on an 18 x 25 figure spends roughly 46% of the visible pixels (180 of
55	390) on contour and bars. That ratio is a property of the figure's size, so the outline
56	decision and the canvas decision are not independent:
57	
58	- On a canvas materially smaller than 32 x 32, a 2 px outline would leave very little
59	  interior for a scout/medic to differ in, and the two characters would be hard to tell
60	  apart.
61	- On a canvas materially larger than 32 x 32, a 2 px outline thins out visually and
62	  reads closer to a 1 px line at the reference's apparent weight.
63	
64	## What the references do not establish
65	
66	- **Projection.** Both figures are front-facing and symmetric. Neither shows a side
67	  view, which is the stated destination. The references establish colour, edge language,
68	  alpha behaviour and detail density; they do not establish the side-view silhouette,
69	  limb construction, or a facing direction.
70	- **Scout and medic differentiation.** Neither reference carries role-identifying
71	  equipment or a distinguishing accent colour.
72	- **Target display scale, engine, or importer.**
73	- **Animation poses, cycles, directions or timing.**
74

1	# Outline and canvas decision brief
2	
3	This is both the decision brief for the project owner and the retained visual
4	observation backing criterion `q_aid_useful` for candidate `x_aid`.
5	
6	- **Sheet:** `deliverables/outline-scale-comparison.png`
7	- **Built from:** the supplied `reference.png` and `reference-b.png` bytes only, enlarged
8	  by integer nearest-neighbour at 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 6x and 8x over light, dark and busy
9	  backgrounds. No content was redrawn or resampled; the accompanying local check
10	  (`evidence/aid-faithfulness.json`) confirmed all 36 panels and 14,040 opaque source
11	  pixels enlarge into uniform blocks with no invented colour.
12	- **Reviewer:** PIXL (agent), viewed in this session, 2026-09-14.
13	- **Outcome for `q_aid_useful`:** pass, with one stated limit.
14	
15	## What the sheet shows
16	
17	**The outline decision is really a background decision.** This is the finding that
18	matters, and it is not visible in either reference on its own.
19	
20	- On the **light** band both treatments read well. The unoutlined teal has ample
21	  contrast against a pale field and needs no help; the outline adds articulation but is
22	  not doing separation work.
23	- On the **dark** band the navy outline is close enough in value to the background that
24	  it partly disappears. The outlined figure reads as a *smaller* teal shape with a soft
25	  dark fringe, and the top stalks nearly vanish because they are entirely outline
26	  colour. The unoutlined figure reads more strongly and holds its full size.
27	- On the **busy** band the relationship inverts. The dark contour is what lifts the
28	  outlined figure off the noisy mid-value field, while the unoutlined teal begins to
29	  blend into it, particularly at the smaller scales.
30	
31	So: if the game's levels are predominantly dark, the outline in `reference.png` actively
32	costs readability. If the levels are busy or mid-value, the outline is what makes the
33	character separable. Choosing the outline without knowing the backgrounds risks picking
34	the treatment that fails where the game actually is.
35	
36	**The outline costs apparent size.** At 6x and 8x the teal interior of the outlined
37	figure is visibly smaller than the full teal body of the unoutlined one. The 2 px
38	contour consumes 180 of 390 visible pixels. On a canvas smaller than the references'
39	32 x 32, that cost grows proportionally and leaves very little interior in which a scout
40	and a medic could differ from one another.
41	
42	**Legibility of the difference by scale.** At 1x the two treatments are not reliably
43	distinguishable — the figure is 18 x 25 device pixels and the outline reads as a general
44	darkening rather than as a contour. At 2x the eyes resolve. From 3x upward the outline
45	treatment is unambiguous. This is the stated limit on the pass: the sheet supports the
46	decision at 3x and above, and shows that at 1x the decision barely matters visually.
47	
48	## What this does not decide
49	
50	The sheet does not choose for you. Per the bundled `edge-rhythm` method, contour style is
51	authored intent and must not be resolved mechanically, and per `silhouette-readability`,
52	no contrast ratio or pixel count proves aesthetic quality. Both treatments are viable;
53	they serve different backgrounds.
54	
55	## Bearing on the canvas choice
56	
57	The two decisions are coupled, so it is worth taking them together:
58	
59	- Keeping the 2 px outline argues for **32 x 32 or larger**, so that interior area
60	  remains for role differentiation between the scout and the medic.
61	- Dropping the outline makes a **smaller canvas** viable, because the full canvas is
62	  available to the figure — but then the shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks that the
63	  navy currently carries have to be re-authored as a second teal value or a cream accent,
64	  or the characters lose those landmarks entirely.

12	NONRASTER = {"code", "report", "reference"}
13	CONTRACT_FIELDS = {"nm", "px", "pl", "vw", "sa", "al", "li", "ch", "tg"}
14	ADOPTION_PHASES = {"production", "delivery"}
15	
16	
17	def _require(condition, code, detail):
18	    if not condition:
19	        raise PixlError(code, detail)
20	
21	
22	def _ids(references):
23	    return {reference.id for reference in references}
24	
25	
26	def _unique(references, code, detail):
27	    _require(len(_ids(references)) == len(references), code, detail)
28	
29	
30	def _output_choices(doc, task):
31	    """Only output contracts impose a task's own project/style obligations.
32	
33	    A source input may intentionally belong to another project or contract.
34	    Unrelated project choices also do not gate research or accepted samples.
35	    """
36	    choices = set()
37	    for output in task["op"]:
38	        contract = doc.records[output.id].fields.get("ct")
39	        if contract is not None:
40	            choices.update(_ids(doc.records[contract.id].fields.get("ch", [])))
41	    return choices
42	
43	
44	def _activation_blockers(doc, task_id, scope, bound):
45	    from . import families
46	
47	    task = doc.records[task_id].fields
48	    reasons = []
49	    for dependency in task["dp"]:
50	        state = doc.records[dependency.id].fields["st"].value
51	        if state != "done":
52	            reasons.append(f"task_prerequisite: {dependency.id} is {state}; it must be done")
53	    for reference in task["op"]:
54	        output = doc.records[reference.id].fields
55	        if output["kd"].value not in NONRASTER and "ct" not in output:
56	            reasons.append(f"output_contract: {reference.id} needs a concrete raster contract")
57	    choice_ids = sorted(_output_choices(doc, task))
58	    for choice_id in choice_ids:
59	        choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
60	        state = choice["st"].value
61	        if state in {"unresolved", "conflict"}:
62	            reasons.append(
63	                f"choice_{state}: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) is {state}; resolve it before active work"
64	            )
65	    if task["ph"].value in ADOPTION_PHASES:
66	        if not task["dc"]:
67	            reasons.append(f"task_decision: {task_id} needs an evidence-backed adoption decision")
68	        for reference in task["kn"]:
69	            method = doc.records[reference.id].fields
70	            if not scope(reference.id) <= bound(method.get("pc", []), passing=True):
71	                reasons.append(f"method_poc: {reference.id} needs current passing method proof")
72	        for choice_id in choice_ids:
73	            choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
74	            if choice["st"].value in {"observed", "proposed"}:
75	                reasons.append(f"choice_unconfirmed: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) must be confirmed")
76	    reasons.extend(families.blockers(doc, task_id))
77	    return reasons

80	def validate(doc, scope, bound):
81	    """Validate PX2 semantics after the graph's shared checks.
82	
83	    ``scope(id)`` returns the semantic proof closure. ``bound(refs, passing)``
84	    returns IDs bound by current receipts. Both are supplied by graph.validate
85	    so lifecycle checks use precisely the same evidence interpretation.
86	    """
87	    choice_keys = set()
88	    current_verdicts = {}
89	
90	    for id_, record in doc.records.items():
91	        f = record.fields
92	        if record.kind == "P":
93	            _unique(f["in"], "intake_project", f"{id_}.in repeats a choice")
94	            for choice in f["in"]:
95	                _require(
96	                    doc.records[choice.id].fields["pr"].id == id_,
97	                    "intake_project", f"{id_}.in includes another project's choice {choice.id}",
98	                )
99	        elif record.kind == "I":
100	            project_id = f["pr"].id
101	            _require(
102	                id_ in _ids(doc.records[project_id].fields["in"]),
103	                "intake_project", f"{id_} must be listed in {project_id}.in",
104	            )
105	            choice_key = (project_id, f["ky"])
106	            _require(
107	                bool(f["ky"].strip()) and choice_key not in choice_keys,
108	                "intake_key", f"{id_}: choice keys must be nonempty and unique within a project",
109	            )
110	            choice_keys.add(choice_key)
111	            state, value = f["st"].value, f["vl"]
112	            if state == "unresolved":
113	                _require(value is None, "intake_value", f"{id_}: unresolved value must be null")
114	            elif state == "conflict":
115	                _require(
116	                    isinstance(value, list) and len(value) >= 2,
117	                    "intake_value", f"{id_}: conflict needs at least two alternatives",
118	                )
119	            else:
120	                _require(value is not None, "intake_value", f"{id_}: {state} value cannot be null")
121	            if state in {"observed", "confirmed"}:
122	                _require(bool(f["so"]), "intake_source", f"{id_}: {state} choice needs sources")
123	            if state == "proposed":
124	                _require(bool(f["wy"].strip()), "intake_rationale", f"{id_}: proposal needs a rationale")
125	        elif record.kind == "C":
126	            _unique(f.get("ch", []), "contract_choice", f"{id_}.ch repeats a choice")
127	            for reference in f.get("ch", []):
128	                choice = doc.records[reference.id].fields
129	                # Retain the last interpretation while an open/blocked task
130	                # resolves changed intent. Activation is gated separately.
131	                if choice["st"].value in {"unresolved", "conflict"}:
132	                    continue
133	                key = choice["ky"]
134	                if key in CONTRACT_FIELDS:
135	                    _require(
136	                        key in f and encode_value(choice["vl"]) == encode_value(f[key]),
137	                        "contract_choice", f"{id_}.{key} does not equal choice {reference.id}",
138	                    )
139	        elif record.kind == "F":
140	            owner = doc.records[f["tk"].id].fields
141	            _require(id_ in _ids(owner["op"]), "output_owner", f"{id_} must be listed by its owning task")
142	            _require(bool(f["rq"]), "output_requirements", f"{id_} needs at least one acceptance criterion")
143	            _unique(f["rq"], "output_requirements", f"{id_}.rq repeats a criterion")
144	        elif record.kind == "Q":
145	            _require(bool(f["ck"].strip()), "criterion_check", f"{id_} needs an observable check")
146	            required_mode = {"visual": "visual", "engine": "live"}.get(f["dm"].value)
147	            _require(
148	                required_mode is None or f["md"].value == required_mode,
149	                "criterion_mode", f"{id_}: {f['dm'].value} requires {required_mode} evidence",
150	            )
151	        elif record.kind == "X":
152	            _require(
153	                f["kd"].value in NONRASTER or "ct" in f,
154	                "artifact_contract", f"{id_}: a materialized raster needs a contract",
155	            )
156	            if "of" in f:
157	                output = doc.records[f["of"].id].fields
158	                _require(
159	                    f["kd"] == output["kd"] and f.get("ct") == output.get("ct"),
160	                    "candidate_output", f"{id_} must match its planned output's kind and contract",
161	                )
162	        elif record.kind == "V":
163	            task = doc.records[f["tk"].id].fields
164	            _require(id_ in _ids(task["vr"]), "verdict_owner", f"{id_} must remain in its task's verdict history")
165	            candidate = doc.records[f["xr"].id].fields
166	            output_ref = candidate.get("of")
167	            _require(output_ref is not None, "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: candidate has no planned output")
168	            output = doc.records[output_ref.id].fields
169	            _require(
170	                output["tk"] == f["tk"] and output_ref.id in _ids(task["op"]),
171	                "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: candidate belongs to another task",
172	            )
173	            try:
174	                datetime.fromisoformat(f["at"])
175	            except ValueError as error:
176	                raise PixlError("date", id_) from error
177	            if f["st"].value == "unavailable":
178	                _require(bool(f["wy"].strip()), "verdict_reason", f"{id_}: explain the unavailable inspection")
179	                _require(not f["ev"], "verdict_unavailable", f"{id_}: unavailable verdict must have no receipts")
180	            if f.get("ob", False):
181	                continue
182	            _require(
183	                f["rq"].id in _ids(output["rq"]),
184	                "verdict_requirement", f"{id_}: criterion is not required by this candidate's output",
185	            )
186	            verdict_key = (f["tk"].id, f["xr"].id, f["rq"].id)
187	            _require(verdict_key not in current_verdicts, "verdict_duplicate", f"{id_}: supersede the previous verdict first")
188	            current_verdicts[verdict_key] = record
189	            if f["st"].value != "unavailable":
190	                current = [e for e in f["ev"] if not doc.records[e.id].fields.get("ob", False)]
191	                criterion = doc.records[f["rq"].id].fields
192	                _require(bool(current), "verdict_evidence", f"{id_}: pass/fail needs current receipts")
193	                _require(
194	                    all(doc.records[e.id].fields["rs"] == f["st"]
195	                        and doc.records[e.id].fields["md"] == criterion["md"] for e in current),
196	                    "verdict_evidence", f"{id_}: receipts must match the verdict outcome and criterion mode",
197	                )
198	                _require(
199	                    scope(f["xr"].id) | scope(f["rq"].id) <= bound(current),
200	                    "verdict_proof", f"{id_}: receipts must bind the exact candidate, criterion and their semantic scopes",
201	                )
202	
203	    for id_, record in doc.records.items():
204	        if record.kind != "T":
205	            continue
206	        f = record.fields
207	        _unique(f["op"], "output_owner", f"{id_}.op repeats a planned output")
208	        _unique(f["vr"], "verdict_owner", f"{id_}.vr repeats a verdict")
209	        for reference in f["op"]:
210	            _require(
211	                doc.records[reference.id].fields["tk"].id == id_,
212	                "output_owner", f"{id_}: {reference.id} belongs to another task",
213	            )
214	        for reference in f["vr"]:
215	            _require(
216	                doc.records[reference.id].fields["tk"].id == id_,
217	                "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: {reference.id} belongs to another task",
218	            )
219	        for choice_id in _output_choices(doc, f):
220	            _require(
221	                doc.records[choice_id].fields["pr"] == f["pr"],
222	                "task_project", f"{id_}: output choice {choice_id} belongs to another project",
223	            )
224	        nominees = {}
225	        for reference in f["ca"]:
226	            candidate = doc.records[reference.id].fields
227	            output = candidate.get("of")
228	            _require(
229	                output is not None and output.id in _ids(f["op"]),
230	                "candidate_output", f"{id_}: nominated {reference.id} must belong to a planned output",
231	            )
232	            _require(
233	                output.id not in nominees, "candidate_nomination",
234	                f"{id_}: only one candidate may be nominated for {output.id}",
235	            )
236	            nominees[output.id] = reference.id
237	        if f["st"].value in {"active", "done"}:
238	            reasons = _activation_blockers(doc, id_, scope, bound)
239	            if reasons:
240	                code, detail = reasons[0].split(": ", 1)
241	                raise PixlError(code, detail)
242	        if f["st"].value == "done":
243	            _require(
244	                bool(f["op"]) and set(nominees) == _ids(f["op"]),
245	                "completion", f"{id_}: every planned output needs one nominated candidate",
246	            )
247	            for output_id, candidate_id in nominees.items():
248	                for requirement in doc.records[output_id].fields["rq"]:
249	                    verdict = current_verdicts.get((id_, candidate_id, requirement.id))
250	                    status = verdict.fields["st"].value if verdict is not None else "unperformed"
251	                    _require(
252	                        status == "pass", "completion",
253	                        f"{id_}: {candidate_id} requirement {requirement.id} is {status}",
254	                    )
255	    return doc
256	
257	
258	def blockers(doc, task_id):
259	    """Return activation blockers for a task in an otherwise valid PX2 graph."""
260	    from .graph import proof_scope
261	
262	    _require(task_id in doc.records and doc.records[task_id].kind == "T", "unknown_task", task_id)
263	
264	    def bound(evidence, passing=False):
265	        covered: set[str] = set()
266	        for reference in evidence:
267	            receipt = doc.records[reference.id].fields
268	            if not receipt.get("ob", False) and (not passing or receipt["rs"].value == "pass"):
269	                covered.update(binding["rf"].id for binding in receipt["bs"])
270	        return covered
271	
272	    return _activation_blockers(doc, task_id, lambda id_: proof_scope(doc, [id_]), bound)
273	
274	
275	def report(doc):
276	    """Describe an already validated PX2 graph without changing its state.
277	
278	    Requirements are shown for each current nominee and for retained older
279	    candidates. An absent current verdict is unperformed, never a pass.
280	    """
281	    intake, tasks, ready = [], [], []
282	    current = {
283	        (r.fields["tk"].id, r.fields["xr"].id, r.fields["rq"].id): r
284	        for r in doc.records.values() if r.kind == "V" and not r.fields.get("ob", False)
285	    }
286	    candidates: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
287	    for id_, record in sorted(doc.records.items()):
288	        if record.kind == "X" and "of" in record.fields:
289	            candidates.setdefault(record.fields["of"].id, []).append(id_)
290	
291	    def requirements(task_id, output, candidate_id):
292	        results = []
293	        for reference in output["rq"]:
294	            criterion = doc.records[reference.id].fields
295	            verdict = current.get((task_id, candidate_id, reference.id))
296	            results.append({
297	                "id": reference.id, "name": criterion["nm"],
298	                "check": criterion["ck"],
299	                "domain": criterion["dm"].value, "mode": criterion["md"].value,
300	                "status": verdict.fields["st"].value if verdict is not None else "unperformed",
301	                "verdict": verdict.id if verdict is not None else None,
302	                "reason": verdict.fields["wy"] if verdict is not None else None,
303	                "reviewer": verdict.fields["wh"].id if verdict is not None else None,
304	                "evidence": [e.id for e in verdict.fields["ev"]] if verdict is not None else [],
305	            })
306	        return results
307	
308	    for id_, record in sorted(doc.records.items()):
309	        f = record.fields
310	        if record.kind == "I":
311	            intake.append({
312	                "id": id_, "project": f["pr"].id, "key": f["ky"],
313	                "status": f["st"].value, "value": to_data(f["vl"]),
314	                "sources": [s.id for s in f["so"]], "rationale": f["wy"],
315	            })
316	        elif record.kind == "T":
317	            reasons = blockers(doc, id_)
318	            if f["st"].value == "open" and not reasons:
319	                ready.append(id_)
320	            nominees = {doc.records[c.id].fields["of"].id: c.id for c in f["ca"]}
321	            outputs = []
322	            for reference in f["op"]:
323	                output = doc.records[reference.id].fields
324	                candidate_id = nominees.get(reference.id)
325	                outputs.append({
326	                    "id": reference.id, "name": output["nm"], "candidate": candidate_id,
327	                    "requirements": requirements(id_, output, candidate_id),
328	                    "candidates": [{
329	                        "id": other, "nominated": other == candidate_id,
330	                        "requirements": requirements(id_, output, other),
331	                    } for other in candidates.get(reference.id, [])],
332	                })
333	            tasks.append({
334	                "id": id_, "project": f["pr"].id, "phase": f["ph"].value,
335	                "state": f["st"].value, "blockers": reasons, "outputs": outputs,
336	            })
337	    return {"intake": intake, "tasks": tasks, "ready": ready}

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. 30	def _output_choices(doc, task):
31	    """Only output contracts impose a task's own project/style obligations.
32	
33	    A source input may intentionally belong to another project or contract.

80	def validate(doc, scope, bound):
81	    """Validate PX2 semantics after the graph's shared checks.
82	
83	    ``scope(id)`` returns the semantic proof closure. ``bound(refs, passing)``
84	    returns IDs bound by current receipts. Both are supplied by graph.validate
85	    so lifecycle checks use precisely the same evidence interpretation.
86	    """
87	    choice_keys = set()
88	    current_verdicts = {}
89	
90	    for id_, record in doc.records.items():
91	        f = record.fields
92	        if record.kind == "P":
93	            _unique(f["in"], "intake_project", f"{id_}.in repeats a choice")
94	            for choice in f["in"]:
95	                _require(
96	                    doc.records[choice.id].fields["pr"].id == id_,
97	                    "intake_project", f"{id_}.in includes another project's choice {choice.id}",
98	                )
99	        elif record.kind == "I":
100	            project_id = f["pr"].id
101	            _require(
102	                id_ in _ids(doc.records[project_id].fields["in"]),
103	                "intake_project", f"{id_} must be listed in {project_id}.in",
104	            )
105	            choice_key = (project_id, f["ky"])
106	            _require(
107	                bool(f["ky"].strip()) and choice_key not in choice_keys,
108	                "intake_key", f"{id_}: choice keys must be nonempty and unique within a project",
109	            )
110	            choice_keys.add(choice_key)
111	            state, value = f["st"].value, f["vl"]
112	            if state == "unresolved":
113	                _require(value is None, "intake_value", f"{id_}: unresolved value must be null")
114	            elif state == "conflict":
115	                _require(
116	                    isinstance(value, list) and len(value) >= 2,
117	                    "intake_value", f"{id_}: conflict needs at least two alternatives",
118	                )
119	            else:
120	                _require(value is not None, "intake_value", f"{id_}: {state} value cannot be null")
121	            if state in {"observed", "confirmed"}:
122	                _require(bool(f["so"]), "intake_source", f"{id_}: {state} choice needs sources")
123	            if state == "proposed":
124	                _require(bool(f["wy"].strip()), "intake_rationale", f"{id_}: proposal needs a rationale")
125	        elif record.kind == "C":
126	            _unique(f.get("ch", []), "contract_choice", f"{id_}.ch repeats a choice")
127	            for reference in f.get("ch", []):
128	                choice = doc.records[reference.id].fields
129	                # Retain the last interpretation while an open/blocked task
130	                # resolves changed intent. Activation is gated separately.
131	                if choice["st"].value in {"unresolved", "conflict"}:
132	                    continue
133	                key = choice["ky"]
134	                if key in CONTRACT_FIELDS:
135	                    _require(
136	                        key in f and encode_value(choice["vl"]) == encode_value(f[key]),
137	                        "contract_choice", f"{id_}.{key} does not equal choice {reference.id}",
138	                    )
139	        elif record.kind == "F":
140	            owner = doc.records[f["tk"].id].fields
141	            _require(id_ in _ids(owner["op"]), "output_owner", f"{id_} must be listed by its owning task")
142	            _require(bool(f["rq"]), "output_requirements", f"{id_} needs at least one acceptance criterion")
143	            _unique(f["rq"], "output_requirements", f"{id_}.rq repeats a criterion")
144	        elif record.kind == "Q":
145	            _require(bool(f["ck"].strip()), "criterion_check", f"{id_} needs an observable check")
146	            required_mode = {"visual": "visual", "engine": "live"}.get(f["dm"].value)
147	            _require(
148	                required_mode is None or f["md"].value == required_mode,
149	                "criterion_mode", f"{id_}: {f['dm'].value} requires {required_mode} evidence",
150	            )
151	        elif record.kind == "X":
152	            _require(
153	                f["kd"].value in NONRASTER or "ct" in f,
154	                "artifact_contract", f"{id_}: a materialized raster needs a contract",
155	            )
156	            if "of" in f:
157	                output = doc.records[f["of"].id].fields
158	                _require(
159	                    f["kd"] == output["kd"] and f.get("ct") == output.get("ct"),
160	                    "candidate_output", f"{id_} must match its planned output's kind and contract",
161	                )
162	        elif record.kind == "V":
163	            task = doc.records[f["tk"].id].fields
164	            _require(id_ in _ids(task["vr"]), "verdict_owner", f"{id_} must remain in its task's verdict history")
165	            candidate = doc.records[f["xr"].id].fields
166	            output_ref = candidate.get("of")
167	            _require(output_ref is not None, "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: candidate has no planned output")
168	            output = doc.records[output_ref.id].fields
169	            _require(
170	                output["tk"] == f["tk"] and output_ref.id in _ids(task["op"]),
171	                "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: candidate belongs to another task",
172	            )
173	            try:

175	            except ValueError as error:
176	                raise PixlError("date", id_) from error
177	            if f["st"].value == "unavailable":

180	            if f.get("ob", False):
181	                continue
182	            _require(
183	                f["rq"].id in _ids(output["rq"]),
184	                "verdict_requirement", f"{id_}: criterion is not required by this candidate's output",

187	            _require(verdict_key not in current_verdicts, "verdict_duplicate", f"{id_}: supersede the previous verdict first")

199	                    scope(f["xr"].id) | scope(f["rq"].id) <= bound(current),

202	
203	    for id_, record in doc.records.items():
204	        if record.kind != "T":
205	            continue
206	        f = record.fields
207	        _unique(f["op"], "output_owner", f"{id_}.op repeats a planned output")
208	        _unique(f["vr"], "verdict_owner", f"{id_}.vr repeats a verdict")
209	        for reference in f["op"]:

214	        for reference in f["vr"]:
215	            _require(
216	                doc.records[reference.id].fields["tk"].id == id_,
217	                "verdict_owner", f"{id_}: {reference.id} belongs to another task",
218	            )
219	        for choice_id in _output_choices(doc, f):
220	            _require(
221	                doc.records[choice_id].fields["pr"] == f["pr"],
222	                "task_project", f"{id_}: output choice {choice_id} belongs to another project",
223	            )
224	        nominees = {}
225	        for reference in f["ca"]:
226	            candidate = doc.records[reference.id].fields
227	            output = candidate.get("of")
228	            _require(
229	                output is not None and output.id in _ids(f["op"]),
230	                "candidate_output", f"{id_}: nominated {reference.id} must belong to a planned output",
231	            )
232	            _require(
233	                output.id not in nominees, "candidate_nomination",
234	                f"{id_}: only one candidate may be nominated for {output.id}",
235	            )
236	            nominees[output.id] = reference.id
237	        if f["st"].value in {"active", "done"}:
238	            reasons = _activation_blockers(doc, id_, scope, bound)
239	            if reasons:

241	                raise PixlError(code, detail)
242	        if f["st"].value == "done":
243	            _require(
244	                bool(f["op"]) and set(nominees) == _ids(f["op"]),

258	def blockers(doc, task_id):
259	    """Return activation blockers for a task in an otherwise valid PX2 graph."""
260	    from .graph import proof_scope
261	
262	    _require(task_id in doc.records and doc.records[task_id].kind == "T", "unknown_task", task_id)
263	
264	    def bound(evidence, passing=False):
265	        covered: set[str] = set()
266	        for reference in evidence:
267	            receipt = doc.records[reference.id].fields
268	            if not receipt.get("ob", False) and (not passing or receipt["rs"].value == "pass"):
269	                covered.update(binding["rf"].id for binding in receipt["bs"])
270	        return covered
271	
272	    return _activation_blockers(doc, task_id, lambda id_: proof_scope(doc, [id_]), bound)

275	def report(doc):
276	    """Describe an already validated PX2 graph without changing its state.
277	
278	    Requirements are shown for each current nominee and for retained older
279	    candidates. An absent current verdict is unperformed, never a pass.
280	    """
281	    intake, tasks, ready = [], [], []
282	    current = {
283	        (r.fields["tk"].id, r.fields["xr"].id, r.fields["rq"].id): r
284	        for r in doc.records.values() if r.kind == "V" and not r.fields.get("ob", False)
285	    }
286	    candidates: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
287	    for id_, record in sorted(doc.records.items()):
288	        if record.kind == "X" and "of" in record.fields:
289	            candidates.setdefault(record.fields["of"].id, []).append(id_)
290	
291	    def requirements(task_id, output, candidate_id):
292	        results = []
293	        for reference in output["rq"]:
294	            criterion = doc.records[reference.id].fields
295	            verdict = current.get((task_id, candidate_id, reference.id))
296	            results.append({
297	                "id": reference.id, "name": criterion["nm"],
298	                "check": criterion["ck"],
299	                "domain": criterion["dm"].value, "mode": criterion["md"].value,
300	                "status": verdict.fields["st"].value if verdict is not None else "unperformed",
301	                "verdict": verdict.id if verdict is not None else None,
302	                "reason": verdict.fields["wy"] if verdict is not None else None,
303	                "reviewer": verdict.fields["wh"].id if verdict is not None else None,
304	                "evidence": [e.id for e in verdict.fields["ev"]] if verdict is not None else [],
305	            })
306	        return results
307	
308	    for id_, record in sorted(doc.records.items()):
309	        f = record.fields
310	        if record.kind == "I":
311	            intake.append({
312	                "id": id_, "project": f["pr"].id, "key": f["ky"],
313	                "status": f["st"].value, "value": to_data(f["vl"]),
314	                "sources": [s.id for s in f["so"]], "rationale": f["wy"],
315	            })
316	        elif record.kind == "T":
317	            reasons = blockers(doc, id_)
318	            if f["st"].value == "open" and not reasons:
319	                ready.append(id_)
320	            nominees = {doc.records[c.id].fields["of"].id: c.id for c in f["ca"]}
321	            outputs = []
322	            for reference in f["op"]:
323	                output = doc.records[reference.id].fields
324	                candidate_id = nominees.get(reference.id)
325	                outputs.append({
326	                    "id": reference.id, "name": output["nm"], "candidate": candidate_id,
327	                    "requirements": requirements(id_, output, candidate_id),
328	                    "candidates": [{
329	                        "id": other, "nominated": other == candidate_id,
330	                        "requirements": requirements(id_, output, other),
331	                    } for other in candidates.get(reference.id, [])],
332	                })
333	            tasks.append({
334	                "id": id_, "project": f["pr"].id, "phase": f["ph"].value,
335	                "state": f["st"].value, "blockers": reasons, "outputs": outputs,
336	            })
337	    return {"intake": intake, "tasks": tasks, "ready": ready}

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Record
88	   **claim or literal criterion; source and locator; current authority/status;
89	   change actually authorized; actual operation prerequisite; finding and
90	   disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted, not just the specialist's
91	   statement that a source supports it. Split mixed-authority clauses. If a
92	   rule rejects a plausible alternative, explain whether the source excludes
93	   that alternative or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve
94	   required outcomes when correcting an unsupported recipe.
95	
96	3. For each requested answer, assume only that answer is supplied and trace
97	   the exact state/contract changes and next available operation. Each other
98	   choice keeps its status unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited
99	   existing decision already establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in
100	   the question, decision table and proposed operation; matching current values
101	   does not prove that a proposed status change is authorized. Check actual
102	   runtime/tool prerequisites and name the dependencies that remain. Scoped
103	   expert proposals can support an authorized sample; do not turn every proposal
104	   into a new owner-confirmation requirement or treat later production
105	   prerequisites as blockers for independent local work.
106	
107	4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
108	   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
109	   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
110	   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
111	   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
112	   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
113	   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.
114	
115	5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
116	   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
117	   affected claims against the sources. Bind your adoption finding to that final
118	   version; a clean summary cannot override contradictory saved criteria or
119	   continuation instructions. Finish with useful saved progress, any still
120	   necessary direct question to the owner, and the concrete operation its answer
121	   enables. Carry existing authorization and leave later prerequisites explicit.
122	
123	## Specialist → caller at completion
124	
125	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
126	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
127	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
128	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
129	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
130	
131	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
132	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
133	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
134	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
135	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
136	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
137	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
138	
139	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
140	
141	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
142	
143	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
144	
145	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
146	
147	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then

149	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The

161	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring

163	
164	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
165	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
166	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
167	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the

170	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
171

173	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
174	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
175	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
176	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
177	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
178	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
179	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
180	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
181	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
182	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
183	not automatically summarized.

186	
187	```json

189	  "status": "partial",
190	  "caller": {
191	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
192	    "integration": {

194	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
195	    },

201	      }

204	}

208	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each

210	JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
211	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
212	`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.
213	
214	Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
215	Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
216	JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
217	truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
218	pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
219	These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
220	after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
221	recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
222	criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.
223	
224	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
225	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and

227	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can

1	# Intake through a reviewed representative sample
2	
3	Use this operation for an incomplete brief, a consequential artistic uncertainty, or the first representative item/pose/cycle/neighborhood before producing a family. Follow the [production profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). This reference governs PIXL operation; maintaining this repository remains a development task.
4	
5	## Required context and entry
6	
7	Read the actual [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New lifecycle projects use `intake STORE --name NAME --brief TEXT --root PROJECT_ROOT`, or `pixl_intake`. It creates a project and actors without a style contract. Existing PX1 state keeps its version; `workflow` deliberately rejects it. Do not relabel an old header, invent past confirmation, or discard old evidence to migrate it.
8	
9	Inspect available references and artifacts at native scale and enlarged scale. Identify which choices affect this operation and which can remain unresolved. Preserve the user's actual instruction or relevant observation in project-owned source files, then record S identities/ranges. The profile supplies the judgment; dimensions, binary alpha and fixed palettes are not universal requirements.
10	
11	## Keep authority through derived rules
12	
13	Before deriving a style contract, acceptance criterion, checker rule or provider instruction, retain a compact account of each consequential restriction: property/value, authority and status, exact supporting instruction or adopted project choice, and where the restriction applies. Use the existing choice/source fields in PIXL state; this account adds no UDL fields. Carry its status through the entire approach, including prompts, checks and handoff.
14	
15	The user's instruction and adopted project choices establish requirements. Reference pixels establish observations; matching a reference does not adopt every measured dimension, color, gap, alpha level or component count as a mandatory rule. For an unspecified property, explain a project-specific proposal and the trial it would test. A proposed trial can proceed within existing authorization while the final production choice remains open.
16	
17	A supplied palette expressed as color roles or families preserves those choices without automatically making sampled reference hex values an exclusive allowed-color list. Use exact working colors as a scoped proposal when useful; attribute exact restrictions to the owner only when their instruction or adoption establishes them. Binary transparency constrains alpha, while opaque edge colors and anti-aliasing require their own authority. Keep these distinctions in the saved contract and criteria, and continue the authorized sample work without asking the caller to repeat settled choices.
18	
19	If your interpretation of an image differs from the brief's terminology, describe the observed pixels and the uncertainty while preserving the requested treatment. An alternative that contradicts that treatment is a change for the user to adopt, not a correction you can silently install in the contract. Neither a tool default nor a passing checker supplies that adoption.
20	
21	Keep diagnostic conclusions attached to their tested artifact, method, scale and background. Failure of one resized fixture does not establish a minimum canvas for other designs; a measured component count or contrast ratio does not establish a universal rejection threshold. Label verified tool limitations separately from artistic choices.
22	
23	Before saving the approach or a verdict, trace every enforced artistic restriction back to that account. Correct downstream claims such as “approved,” “binding,” or “must” when their source is still observed, proposed or unresolved. Preserve the earlier draft and its evidence when correcting it.
24	
25	For a selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate, use [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed output/criteria plan and first durable request in one operation. The record-level sequence below remains available for advanced plans and explicit amendments.
26	
27	## Preserve intake and plan before execution
28	
29	1. Load the current state and canonical hash. Decode it through the runner, keeping `format: 2` in the host adapter. Amend the relevant fields, increase the revision by one, encode a candidate, validate against the project root, and commit with the previously observed hash. A stale-write error means reload and reconcile.
30	2. Add each consequential choice as I with project, actor, key, status, value, sources and rationale; add it to P.in. Unknown values are null. Observations, proposals and confirmations remain different statuses. Preserve conflicting alternatives instead of selecting a scaffold default.
31	3. Research the uncertain technique through the [knowledge operation](knowledge.md). A K recipe or reference POC is useful context, not a proof for this asset. A research/sample T can use unproven K and have `dc=[]`; it does not need a fabricated D. Adoption into production/delivery needs the specified decision and applicable proofs.
32	4. Name the smallest useful sample as F, owned by its T. Separate T.ip inputs, T.op planned outputs and T.ca actual nominated candidates. Before a file exists, F is the output plan; do not create a false X path/hash. Instantiate a concrete C only from usable observed/proposed/confirmed choices. Link those choices through C.ch. An unresolved canvas can remain I while a raster F has no C and its sample task is blocked.
33	5. Declare Q criteria appropriate to the question and destination. Include explicit observable conditions, domain and required evidence mode. Mechanical properties, visual readability, temporal/neighbor continuity and engine behavior are separate where applicable. Do not add irrelevant gates to a report or impose a universal art style. Save this plan before interpreting candidate results: new pass/fail verdicts require the same plan and semantic scope in the prior saved revision.
34	
35	The bundled [incomplete intake example](../../../resources/examples/intake/project.px) shows declared choices, a planned output and requirements without a fabricated artifact. It is a syntax example, not a project-approved style or a finished sample.
36	
37	Host adapter example for one unresolved choice (add a real P reference and actor; this is one record, not a complete document):
38	
39	```json
40	{"id":"canvas","kind":"I","fields":{"pr":{"$ref":"project"},"wh":{"$ref":"user"},"ky":"px","st":{"$symbol":"unresolved"},"vl":null,"so":[],"wy":"The final canvas size has not been chosen."}}
41	```
